aliases: N-doped graphene-decorated NiCo alloy coupled with mesoporous NiCoMoO nano-sheet grown on 3D nickel foam

nodes.name: Nickel foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam (NF, 2.0 × 4.0 cm²) was treated in ethanol, 3.0 M hydrochloric acid, and ultrapure water with ultrasonication, respectively.
nodes.source_text: First, nickel foam (NF, 2.0 × 4.0 cm²) was treated in ethanol, 3.0 M hydrochloric acid, and ultrapure water with ultrasonication, respectively.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of NiCoMoO precursor
nodes.procedure: The cleaned NF was put in a 30 mL mix solution (ethylene glycol and ultra-pure water) with sodium molybdate dihydrate, urea, and nitrate hexahydrate. The mix solution was put into steel autoclave for 12 h at 180 °C. After cooling to 25 °C, the NF was washed by ethanol and ultrapure water, and dried overnight under vacuum at 80 °C.

Third, the mix solution was put into steel autoclave for 12 h at 180 °C. After cooling to 25 °C, the NF was washed by ethanol and ultrapure water, and dried overnight under vacuum at 80 °C.

nodes.name: Annealing to form NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF
nodes.procedure: The dried sample was treated at 450 °C under 5% H₂ + 95% Ar atmosphere for 2 h (3 °C min⁻¹), the obtained sample named as NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF, and its mass load on NF was ≈10.5 mg cm⁻².

unit_operations.name: Annealing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the dried sample was treated at 450 °C under 5% H₂ + 95% Ar atmosphere for 2 h (3 °C min⁻¹)

nodes.source_text: Finally, the dried sample was treated at 450 °C under 5% H₂ + 95% Ar atmosphere for 2 h (3 °C min⁻¹, the obtained sample named as NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF)

nodes.source_text: The HER electrocatalytic activity of the samples is evaluated by a three-electrode system under 1.0 M KOH solution containing saturated N₂. Obviously, the NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF only acquires low overpotentials of 39 and 266 mV at −10 and −1000 mA cm⁻²... which displays excellent stability after continuous work 340 h, and the potential has only changed 18 mV.
NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF has the low overpotentials (260 and 390 mV) at 10 and 1000 mA cm⁻²... NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF can keep for 340 h at 1000 mA cm⁻², and the change of potential is 12 mV.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1.0 M KOH at 30°C
nodes.source_text: at 100 mA cm⁻², under 1.0 M KOH solution at 30 °C, WE performance of NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF (1.71 V)... only requires a low potential of 2.01 V to deliver 1000 mA cm⁻² and perform for 295 h with negligible change 50 mV... the volume ratio of H₂ and O₂ is about 2:1, which is consistent with theoretical values, suggesting the closely 100% Faradic efficiency.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 6.0 M KOH at 60°C

nodes.name: NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF
aliases: N-doped graphene-decorated NiCo alloy coupled with mesoporous NiCoMoO nano-sheet

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show nanoparticles uniformly anchored on self-supported mesoporous nano-sheet, different from smooth-surfaced NiCo-MoO nano-sheet precursors.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S1a, b displays the SEM images of NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF (annealed at 450 °C), which shows that the nanoparticles are uniformly anchored on the self-supported mesoporous nano-sheet, and it is different from the NiCo-MoO nano-sheet precursors with smooth surfaces (Fig. S1c, d).

properties.label: C
properties.description: High-resolution image showing dense distribution of nanoparticles with scale bar of 100 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows diffraction peaks at (111), (200), and (220) planes of NiCo alloy, and other peaks assigned to Ni₂Mo₃O₈ (PDF#37-0855) and Co₂Mo₃O₈ (PDF#34-0511).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD images in Fig. S2 show that the three diffraction peaks belong to the (111), (200), and (220) planes of NiCo, respectively. Furthermore, the other peaks can be assigned to Ni₂Mo₃O₈ (PDF#37-0855) and Co₂Mo₃O₈ (PDF#34-0511).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals nanoparticles (≈30-50 nm) evenly dispersed on mesoporous nano-sheet (2-15 nm pores); HRTEM shows interplanar distances of 0.209 nm (111) NiCo, 0.248 nm (112) Ni₂Mo₃O₈, 0.260 nm (200) Co₂Mo₃O₈; NiCo alloy coated by ~4 layers graphene.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM, high-angle annular dark field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM), and high resolution TEM (HRTEM) images (Fig. 2a–g) are used to reveal the lattice fringe, N-doped graphene, mesoporous nano-sheet, and nanoparticles (≈30-50 nm) structure. The nanoparticles are evenly dispersed on the mesoporous nano-sheet (Fig. 2a). In Fig. 2b–d, the interplanar distances of 0.209 nm (111), 0.248 nm (112), and 0.260 nm (200) are assigned to NiCo, Ni₂Mo₃O₈, and Co₂Mo₃O₈... the NiCo alloy is obviously coated by graphene carbon (~ 4 layers) in Fig. 2e...

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with porous morphology and bright contrast features

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows ID/IG ratio of 1.36 at 450 °C, indicating larger number of structural defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The graphene carbon of NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF is also evaluated by Raman in Fig. S3, and the ratio of area D and G is 1.36 at 450 °C...

nodes.characterization_summary: BET analysis shows specific surface area 102.96 m²/g, pore volume 0.18 cm³/g, average pore size 6.83 nm; most mesoporous peaks range 1.0-14.0 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the pore volume/size (0.18 cm³ g⁻¹/6.83 nm) and specific surface area (102.96 m² g⁻¹) are characterized by N₂ absorption/desorption measurements, and the most parts range of mesoporous peaks is 1.0-14.0 nm (Fig. S5a, b and Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks with ≈0.4 eV positive shift, Co 2p peaks with ≈0.5 eV positive shift compared to NiCo-NiCoMoO/NF; Mo 3d fitted to Mo⁶⁺ (235.1/232.0), Mo⁵⁺ (233.3/230.2), Mo⁴⁺ (232.5/229.4); C 1s at C=O (288.4 eV), C–N (286.2 eV), C–C (284.8 eV); N 1s at graphitic-N (401.3 eV) and pyridinic-N (398.5 eV); O 1s at absorbed-O (532.4 eV) and NiCoMo-O (530.7 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Subsequently, the electron interaction and elemental status of Ni, Co, Mo, O, C, and N elements in NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF (Figs. 3 and S7) are proved by XPS.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mappings demonstrate Ni, Co, Mo, O, C, and N elements evenly distributed on NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF nano-sheet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS elemental mappings (Fig. 2h–m) demonstrate that the Ni, Co, Mo, O, C, and N elements are evenly distributed on NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF nano-sheet.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms mesoporous structure (2-15 nm) of NiCo@C-NiCoMoO/NF nano-sheet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: it also exhibits mesoporous structure (2-15 nm) in Figs. 2b, c and S4a–c, which can be obtained by HAADF-STEM (Figs. 2f and S4d, e).
